title: The Last Standard Bearer
subtitle: Yajna Sri Śātakarṇi and the final flare of Satavahana power
era: Late Satavahana power, c. 152-203 CE depending on chronology
region: Kanheri, Nasik, Nagarjunakonda and the Deccan coasts
moral: A final rally can shine even as an old order fades.

sources.citation: James Burgess, Report on the Buddhist Cave Temples and Their Inscriptions (ASI, 1882)
sources.note: Kanheri inscriptions and western Deccan cave records.

sources.citation: E. Senart, 'Inscriptions at Nasik,' Epigraphia Indica Vol. 8 (1905)
sources.note: Nasik Cave 20 and related late Satavahana records.

sources.citation: Akira Shimada, Early Buddhist Architecture in Context (Brill, 2012)
sources.note: Recent chronology linking late Satavahanas, Amaravati and regional transitions.

dialogue.text: In the fading light of Satavahana power, Yajna Sri Śātakarṇi rises as the last great standard bearer of a vast Deccan realm.
For generations the Satavahanas ruled the Deccan, binding plateau and coast, craftsman and caravan, monk and cultivator in a long, shifting web of power.

panels.shot: slow push-in on a weathered stone inscription

dialogue.text: When chronicles fall silent, stone remembers. At Kanheri and Nasik, chiseled letters speak of Yajna Sri Śātakarṇi’s name and reach.

panels.shot: medium shot at court, slight low angle

dialogue.text: He does not rise in a vacuum. Earlier Satavahana kings had strained against western Satraps, clashing and yielding ground long before his own time.

panels.shot: split composition showing Deccan plateau on one side and western coastal line on the other

dialogue.text: By Yajna Sri’s age, Satavahana strength had stretched and thinned. Western tracts near the coast saw Satrap pressure, local chiefs sensed opportunity, and unity frayed.

panels.shot: tight three-quarter profile on Yajna Sri, contemplative

dialogue.speaker: yajna_sri_satakarni
dialogue.text: The west cannot be abandoned. Our standards must be seen there once more.

panels.shot: epic wide shot of marching columns

dialogue.text: He rallies what strength remains, pushing westward along ancient routes, reasserting Satavahana presence where rival flags had begun to flicker.

panels.shot: medium shot in front of a cave façade

dialogue.text: At Nasik, his name is carved into grants for caves and monasteries, a sign that Satavahana authority has once more brushed these western valleys.

panels.shot: close-up on hands holding a copper plate or stone grant

dialogue.text: These donations do more than express piety. They declare, to merchants and monks alike, whose protection shields the caves and roads.
Far from his inland base, Kanheri’s inscriptions speak of his shadow on the coastal hills near the western sea lanes.

panels.shot: close shot of Satavahana coin resting on cloth

dialogue.text: On coins linked to his age, ships sail in miniature relief. They hint at rulers who understand the lifeblood of coasts and long sea routes.

panels.shot: wide shot of a busy port scene

dialogue.text: Satavahana power does not float on fleets alone, but it leans on ports, on the taxes of goods, and on the safe passage of those who travel by river and sea.

panels.shot: somber interior shot in a royal audience hall

dialogue.text: Yet even as Yajna Sri extends his reach, centrifugal forces grow. Local elites weigh their loyalties, imagining futures with their own emblems raised high.

panels.shot: close-up on Yajna Sri’s face in half-shadow

dialogue.speaker: yajna_sri_satakarni
dialogue.text: A king can reclaim ground, not youth for an old house.

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot with ghosted banners of different dynasties rising

dialogue.text: After his time, the once-broad realm fragments. Abhira chiefs, Ikshvaku rulers, Chutu lords and others claim pieces of the Deccan, forging successor states.

panels.shot: wide shot of Nagarjunakonda valley and river

dialogue.text: In places like Nagarjunakonda, new powers build and patronize, while memories of Satavahana kings linger in stone, coin, and the alignment of routes they once guarded.

panels.shot: slow pan across cave interiors with multiple inscription panels

dialogue.text: Historians read these scattered records, tracing how his grants mark a late peak, and how later lines chart the shift to new dynasties and patrons.

panels.shot: heroic but wistful medium shot on Yajna Sri against an evening sky

dialogue.text: He is remembered not as the founder, nor as the conqueror of all, but as the last great Satavahana who gathered what remained and made it blaze once more.

panels.shot: final pull-back from Deccan landscape into starry night

dialogue.text: His story teaches that even as an order dissolves, a last rally can steady roads, honor old bonds, and leave marks in stone and memory that endure beyond a dynasty’s fall.
